claims.text: A conventionally processed HfNbTaTiZr-type refractory high-entropy alloy has a homogeneous microstructure without secondary-phase dispersions.
Mechanical alloying followed by spark plasma sintering can introduce a nanoscale Y2O3 dispersion into the refractory high-entropy alloy.
Process optimization and microstructural characterization can produce a uniform and stable distribution of Y2O3 particles.
The introduced Y2O3 nanoparticles will be distributed both at grain boundaries and within grains.
Y2O3 nanoparticles act as stable sinks for irradiation-induced defects.
Y2O3 nanoparticles trap radiation-induced vacancies and interstitials.
Trapping vacancies and interstitials at Y2O3 nanoparticles promotes defect annihilation and reduces the formation of defect clusters.
Reduced point-defect clustering decreases irradiation-induced void and bubble formation.
Y2O3 nanoparticles inhibit grain growth during thermal transients.
Inhibition of grain growth preserves a refined microstructure and maintains mechanical strength.
The Y2O3-modified alloy will exhibit at least 30% less irradiation-induced swelling than the unmodified alloy.
The Y2O3-modified alloy will have lower post-irradiation void and bubble density than the unmodified alloy.
The Y2O3-modified alloy will preserve yield strength under the stated irradiation conditions.
The Y2O3-modified alloy will preserve ductility under the stated irradiation conditions.
The predicted radiation-tolerance benefits apply at 600–800 °C under helium implantation and neutron exposure representative of plasma-facing service.
The efficacy of the Y2O3 dispersion outside the specified temperature and flux conditions has not been established.
